title: Getting Oriented
answer: The first four chapters lay the foundation for everything that follows. They explain what AI can and cannot do, the ten patterns that account for nearly every idea in the Volume, the laws and rules that protect students, and a simple method for piloting and measuring any new tool.

children.name: What AI Can and Cannot Do
children.blurb: In the fall of 2023, nearly 1,000 students at a high school in Turkey took part in a simple test. During math review sessions, some students practiced with a plain AI chat tool, much like the free chatbots anyone can open on a phone.

children.name: Ten Patterns That Show Up Everywhere
children.blurb: When this Volume began, the raw material was a stack of 1,200 ideas for using AI in schools, gathered from teachers, district leaders, researchers, and product lists. Reading them one by one felt like walking through a crowded market where every stall sold something slightly different.

children.name: Privacy, Safety, and the Human Review Rule
children.blurb: In June 2026, a school board member in Portland, Oregon, raised concerns about the data an AI reading assessment company would collect from students. The list of data fields in the company's contract included items such as place of birth and migrant status (Willamette Week, 2026).

children.name: Pilot, Measure, Scale
children.blurb: In a recent trial in Germany, 371 students in grades 7 through 9 used generative AI tools during six regular physics and English lessons. Some students got a tool designed to build motivation, some got a tool designed to teach learning strategies, and a comparison group used a plain chatbot.

sections.body: Getting Oriented is the opening part of the book, where the foundation for everything else is laid. It covers what AI can and cannot do, the ten patterns that account for nearly every idea in the Volume, the laws and rules that protect students, and a simple method for piloting and measuring any new tool. The book says readers who start nowhere else should start here. The rules set out in these chapters apply to every idea in the chapters that follow.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The book holds that this foundation works because it gives readers a shared basis before they meet any tool or idea. It does not present these chapters as optional background, and it warns that the rules in them apply throughout the rest of the Volume. The rule it holds to is that anyone starting out should begin here rather than somewhere else. What does not work, by implication, is skipping this ground and going straight to later ideas.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The four pages fit together as a sequence from understanding to practice. What AI Can and Cannot Do sets the honest limits of the technology, and Ten Patterns That Show Up Everywhere gives the recurring ideas that account for nearly every concept in the Volume. Privacy, Safety, and the Human Review Rule carries the laws and rules that protect students, and Pilot, Measure, Scale offers the simple method for trying and judging any new tool. A teacher would go to the first two for understanding, a leader to the third for the rules, and a parent or leader to the fourth for how a tool is tested before it is trusted.
